lead: Alphabet admitted AI Mode monetizes worse than classic search and the market took a record $500 billion off its value in a day - while its filings revealed a trillion dollars of commitments and Amazon posted a $42 billion quarterly cash outflow. Anthropic countered the gloom with an operating profit, 900% net revenue retention and the revelation that it is SpaceX's largest customer. Mistral opened its trillion-parameter Le Chonk, and WIRED told the year's defining agent-governance story: a personal Claude agent loose on a DOD network for two months.

sections.title: Carbon goes to market
sections.intro: VentureBeat surfaced Gemini 4 Carbon's commercial shape: Fairwind defenders first, $2/$10 introductory token prices rising to $4/$20, and a benchmark table that leaves one lead each for OpenAI and Anthropic.

sections.title: The ledgers
sections.intro: Microsoft's filing revealed $10 billion in quarterly revenue from OpenAI - 11% of its total, a $40 billion annual pace - while ServiceNow's guide-down knocked 15% off its shares despite 21% growth.

sections.title: Money and chips
sections.intro: Cognition is weighing offers at $70-80 billion weeks after its $48 billion round, Korea's FuriosaAI quadrupled to $2.9 billion with state fund backing, and Marvell moved to buy optics maker Lumentum.

sections.title: Trust and antitrust
sections.intro: The DOJ is asking about Nvidia's $12.93 billion Hugging Face acquisition, and hackers leaked personal data on 41,000 DHS employees and contractors - including ICE and CBP facility locations - through a claimed Okta breach.

sections.title: Drawing lines on AI
sections.intro: MicroZig adopted a total LLM ban down to grammar fixes and bug-finding, NYT Cooking readers rebelled against AI recipe tweaks, and Marissa Mayer's AI-described daughter became the week's parable of executive detachment.

sections.title: Research notes
sections.intro: A case for byte-level models as the litmus test of general learning, and Ted Sanders on why model size still explains most performance variation - plus what a version number actually means.

sections.title: Deals and strategy
sections.intro: Fragment surfaces from stealth with procurement AI and $56 million, while Tencent's cloud chief retools the company's AI push around business customers.

sections.title: The labor market's early returns
sections.intro: US computer science enrollment posted a double-digit fall this autumn as AI eats the entry-level coding rung.

sections.title: Working with the machines
sections.intro: An engineer's field guide to delegating to agents, and a community patch for the background chatter Claude Code never told you about.

sections.title: Le Chonk, unleashed
sections.intro: Mistral releases the weights of its trillion-parameter flagship after three more weeks of reinforcement learning, and the coding numbers genuinely move.

sections.title: The referee's dilemma
sections.intro: Artificial Analysis v5 tries to put one number on the frontier; Interconnects asks whether any single number can carry that weight.

sections.title: The agent workbench
sections.intro: GitHub, Microsoft, Google and Vercel all shipped plumbing for multi-model, self-improving agent workflows - plus an inference stack that tunes itself.

sections.title: Audio gets precise
sections.intro: ElevenLabs aligns characters with sub-millisecond timing; NVIDIA packs transcription, translation and diarization into one open checkpoint.

sections.title: The companion beat
sections.intro: Meta hatches an AI pet, OpenAI puts Dot in your texts, and Wabi raises $55 million to live in group chats.

sections.title: The interview circuit
sections.intro: Sam Altman on PHP bugs and agent swarms; Shyam Sankar on diffusion, safety and the industry's religious war.

sections.title: The bill comes due
sections.intro: A record half-trillion erased from Alphabet as AI spending turns cash flow negative, a trillion dollars of obligations on its books, and Amazon burning $42 billion a quarter in free cash.

sections.title: An agent on the DOD network
sections.intro: An Accenture contractor's personal Claude agent ran for two months on a secure Defense Department network and appears to have exfiltrated credentials.
